counterfactual_missing_items: No raw span documents AHO features such as brachydactyly, round face, or subcutaneous ossifications to support type 1A
No raw span documents normal calcium or PTH, which would be required for idiopathic basal ganglia calcification
No raw span establishes epilepsy as a primary diagnosis rather than a manifestation of hypocalcemia
decisive_items: Transverse CT scan of the head showing bilateral hyperdense areas in the basal ganglia and frontal lobes
response.rationale: R1 is the best fit: hypocalcemia with elevated PTH and brain calcification in a young adult with seizure identifies pseudohypoparathyroidism. C1 shares the same core raw spans but adds an unsupported subtype; R2 uses only the CT calcification and ignores the abnormal calcium/PTH; R3 captures only the seizure symptom.

rejected.why: The CT calcification is present, but the low calcium and elevated PTH are incompatible with idiopathic basal ganglia calcification, which requires normal mineral metabolism.
Seizure and EEG changes are symptoms of the underlying metabolic disorder, not the most likely diagnosis; the raw labs and imaging provide the causal diagnosis.
